requirements.quote: At least two templates per launch court (mention or adjournment memo, client covering letter) plus the other listed kinds exist, each with `is_system = true` and a stable id [type:unit]
Seeding is idempotent: running it twice produces no duplicate rows and updates a template only when its checksum changes [type:api]
Each template renders with the Madras HC or Karnataka HC preset from #75 and passes a snapshot test using the synthetic demo data with fictional parties [type:unit]
Case-type labels, hall and bench phrases come from the adapter catalogue and are not hard-coded strings in templates [type:unit]
Client covering letter slots only read data about an existing client of the workspace; it never offers a field for non-client recipients [type:unit]
Every template shows a visible banner `Scaffold: review before use` until its `reviewed_by` metadata is set, and exporting records the banner state in the audit event [type:unit]
Templates contain no pre-filled legal citations or authorities; a lint test fails if a citation-pattern string appears in a system template [type:unit]
The covering letter and memo contain no advice, no commitment, no fee quote and no solicitation language; a phrase lint (denylist) runs in CI [type:unit]
Tamil or Kannada content language switches the font fallback in DOCX and PDF output and renders glyphs without tofu [type:manual]
Templates are read-only to workspaces (SELECT policy only); copying into a workspace template creates a new row owned by that workspace [type:api]
i18n: all template labels used in the UI have `en` keys and `ta`/`kn` stubs [type:unit]
the routine documents lawyers actually produce (early-listing memo, memo of appearance, application for certified copy, request for adjournment note, covering letter to junior or senior counsel).
requirements.why: The v1 catalogue table lists no counsel covering letter, and it needs a non-client recipient slot that the client-letter rule forbids; file as a follow-up with its own recipient model.
